events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
This is a no-show cancellation-fee dispute. The driver cancelled (F4), so the fee can only stand through NS-0 → NS-1, which requires cumulatively: (i) an "I'm Here" press, (ii) GPS presence at the pickup at the moment of the press, and (iii) more than 3 minutes of waiting at the pickup after that press [NS-0][NS-1].

On the tap, the record is internally inconsistent: F7 says driver_pressed_here_at is null, while F6 records a tap at 13:02:45. The execution trace resolves this in the driver's favour — (i) and (ii) pass (tap at 13:02:45, 41 m from pickup) — and I accept that resolution [F6][F1][NS-1]. The clock therefore starts at 13:02:45, not at the platform's auto-arrival marker of 13:01:10.

From the tap, the driver stayed inside the 200 m radius for only 175 s (2 min 55 s) before cancelling at 13:05:40 [F6][F4]. NS-1 (iii) requires strictly more than 3 minutes (≥ 3:01). 175 s < 181 s, so requirement (iii) fails [F6][F4][NS-1]. The driver's physical presence (closest approach 38 m at 13:04:30; stationary 3 min 15 s from 13:02:25) and the platform's 4 min 30 s "arrival to cancellation" interval do not cure this, because both are measured before the tap event from which NS-1 (iii) runs [F1][F2][F3][F5][NS-1].

With any one of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) unmet, NS-2 mandates a full refund of the $6.61 cancellation fee [F8][NS-2][NS-1]. Amount = cancellation fee on record $6.61 [F8][NS-2].

No account flag is warranted: the trace finds no fake tap (the driver was 41 m from pickup when he tapped), and both profiles show 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days, so neither RD-6 nor the NS-2 flag branch is triggered [F6][F1][F16][F17][NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag on either party.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee charged to my client rests on the driver's no-show claim, but the system timeline shows the driver never pressed "I'm Here": F7 records driver_pressed_here_at as null, contradicting the driver's statement in F12.

NS-1 requires both (i) the "I'm Here" tap and (iii) more than 3 minutes of waiting at the pickup point; with no tap on record (F7) requirement (i) fails outright, and the fee cannot be upheld even though F2/F3 show the driver physically close to the pickup.
Where NS-1 is not satisfied, NS-2 requires the cancellation fee to be refunded in full; the recorded fee of $6.61 (F8) is therefore fully refundable to my client.

The driver's own messages corroborate the fee's invalidity: he announced "I'm here" at 13:02 (F10) and cancelled at 13:05 (F11), i.e. only 2 min 55 s of in-range presence after his claimed arrival marker, which falls short of the >3-minute wait NS-1 (iii) requires.

My client had no surge-driven exposure and no other published add-on justifying the charge: the trip carried a 1.0x surge multiplier (F9) and the only amount in dispute is the $6.61 cancellation fee (F8).

Nothing in the trip conditions excuses the cancellation without the required I'm-Here precondition: fair weather (F15) and no traffic incidents near the route (F14) mean no operational reason distorted the arrival process.

weaknesses: The strongest facts for the driver are F2, F3 and F6: he was within 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 4 min 30 s, stationary 3 min 15 s at 40 m, and F6 records a "I'm Here" tap at 13:02:45 — 41 m from the pickup — which, if credited, would satisfy NS-1 (i) and (ii).

F6 and F7 are timeline facts that directly contradict each other on whether the "I'm Here" button was pressed (F6 gives 13:02:45; F7 says null); the judge may prefer F6 and, combined with F2/F3/F5, could find NS-1 fully satisfied and the fee valid.

My client's own statement ("came out a minute after the driver cancelled") is a statement only; the system records in F3/F4 show the driver stationary from 13:02:25 to 13:05:40 and cancelling at 13:05:40, so on the record my client was still inside the pickup area for the full 3+ minutes the driver waited.

F14 and F13 show no incident but ordinary band-3 traffic (20-29 km/h) on Tampines Street 82, which the other side may cite as an operational excuse for the sequence of events, though it does not cure the missing NS-1 (i) precondition.
Neither party has any prior dispute history (F16, F17), so no RD-6/NS-2 flag_account enhancement is available on these facts.

claims.assertion: The driver physically reached the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m from the pickup at 13:04:30 and he was first inside 200 m at 13:01:10, satisfying the 'at the pick-up location according to GPS data' requirement.

The driver waited well over the 3-minute threshold: he was inside 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 4 min 30 s before cancelling, and the platform's own timeline records 4 min 30 s between recorded arrival and cancellation.
The driver was stationary at the pickup point for 3 min 15 s (13:02:25–13:05:40), 40 m from the pickup point — a continuous stationary wait exceeding 3:01 within 200 m.

The driver announced his presence to the rider in-app at 13:02 ('I'm here at the pickup point, white Honda Vezel') and only cancelled at 13:05:40 after stating he had waited more than 3 minutes, so the rider had notice of the wait before the fee was incurred.
Because all NS-1 conditions are met, the $6.61 cancellation fee stands as charged on the record and the correct outcome for this dispute is no_action, with $4.50 payable to the driver.

The rider's claim of arriving 'a minute after' cancellation is not supported by any system record: the fare shows only the flat $6.61 fee with no surge component, so there is no computable overcharge to refund.

weaknesses: F7 (timeline) states the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), which contradicts F6 (tap at 13:02:45) and the driver's own statement F12; NS-1 (i) requires the 'I'm Here' press, so the rider will argue the requirement fails and NS-2 requires a full $6.61 refund. My answer rests on F2/F3/F5 (the system wait record) rather than on the disputed tap.

The rider's complaint that he came out 'a minute after' cancellation is a statement with no GPS/timeline fact of the rider at the pickup point in the table, so I cannot rebut it with a rider-side system record — only with the driver-side wait facts F2, F3 and F5.
F17 shows the driver has 0 prior disputes and 0 upheld, so the RD-6-style 'repeated' account flag is unavailable; no aggravating profile fact supports a flag_account add-on here.

points.response: D1 argues NS-1 (ii) only; NS-1 requires (i), (ii) AND (iii) cumulatively, and the system timeline F7 records driver_pressed_here_at as null, so the location showing in F1/F2 cannot cure the missing precondition. A driver who was physically there but never signaled 'I'm Here' has not met NS-1, and NS-2 then mandates a full refund.

D2's wait record (F2, F5) is a system fact, but a factual wait only matters under NS-1 (iii) if the button requirement in NS-1 (i) is also met; F7 shows no 'I'm Here' event ever occurred, so the 4 min 30 s inside 200 m is legally inert.

The 3 min 15 s stationary period in F3 starts at 13:02:25, which is before — not after — the F6 tap time of 13:02:45, and F6 itself only records 2 min 55 s of in-range presence after the claimed tap, so even on the driver's own best case the NS-1 (iii) threshold of over 3 minutes measured from the tap is not met.

A chat message ('I'm here' at 13:02, F10) is user-submitted content and cannot substitute for the system's button event required by NS-1 (i); F7, a timeline record, is the system record and it says no tap occurred, and under NS-1 the driver must both press 'I'm Here' and be at the pickup per GPS — notice by chat is not one of the enumerated conditions.

D5 concludes that all NS-1 conditions are met, but it never addresses NS-1 (i): F7 records no 'I'm Here' press and the driver's own statement F12 claims one, so the premise fails and NS-2 requires the $6.61 in F8 to be refunded in full rather than no_action.

D6 misstates my case: I do not claim an overcharge beyond the fee, I claim the flat $6.61 (F8) was charged without NS-1 (i) being satisfied (F7), and NS-2 makes that fee refundable regardless of the 1.0x multiplier in F9.

I refine my own C4: the 2 min 55 s figure from F6 matters only if the F6 tap is credited, so the driver's position is protected primarily by F7, which denies any tap ever happened and leaves NS-1 (i) unsatisfied.

Conceded in part: I accept that F2 and F5 establish a genuine 4 min 30 s in-range wait by the driver, and F3 a 3 min 15 s stationary period; my case does not depend on denying those records, only on the missing NS-1 (i) precondition.

F7 is a single timeline field, while F6 in the same timeline records a recorded "I'm Here" tap at 13:02:45 with the driver 41 m from the pickup; on the stronger reading of the record the tap occurred, and in any event the wait requirement is proved independently by F2/F3/F5.

Even if the tap is disputed, the substantive NS-1 precondition (ii) and the wait duration are established by system records the rider does not contest: F2 (first within 200 m at 13:01:10, 4 min 30 s cumulative inside 200 m) and F3 (stationary 3 min 15 s, 40 m from pickup), as the opposing brief itself concedes.
NS-2 only triggers where NS-1 (i), (ii) or (iii) fails; on F2/F3/F5 the location and the greater-than-3-minute wait are met, so the recorded $6.61 fee (F8) is valid and no refund follows.

The rider's 2 min 55 s figure is measured only from the 13:02:45 tap in F6; the correct measure is F2, which shows the driver inside 200 m from 13:01:10 for a cumulative 4 min 30 s, and F5, which records cancellation 4 min 30 s after arrival — both above the 3:01 threshold.

The rider's own point confirms the only disputed item is the $6.61 cancellation fee (F8) with no surge (F9); that fee is exactly the published cancellation fee under NS-0/NS-1 and therefore stands rather than being refunded.

Fair weather (F15) and no incidents near the route (F14) do not make the fee invalid; the charge is justified by the driver's documented wait at the pickup point (F2, F3) regardless of traffic or weather conditions.
I withdraw nothing, but note the record supports the driver's presence: F1 places his closest approach at 38 m and F2 at 13:01:10 inside 200 m, so the location precondition is not seriously in doubt.
